rubric_notes: Complete. Verified release/freeze dates, a.22 single superfamily, homology endpoint, five families with sunids and members, 'not a true family' comment, duplication/PF09123, linker histone a.4.5.13 lineage with PF00538 annotation, and enzyme search hits. Clear level-by-level reading (family < superfamily; class says nothing), explicit refusal to transfer nucleosome function/templates, caveats on automated matches and partial search, and separates general-knowledge background from API facts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All classifications, sunids, boundaries (1vmg A: whole chain; 1y6x A:7-93), annotations (structural genomics, Li/UNL) and sibling families supported by bundle. Superfamily-level remote homology stated with correct caveat that absence of warnings is not extra evidence. Rejects both directions of function transfer, notes MazG-like is a label not a demonstrated activity, and lists needed external evidence (assays, alignment). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

All identifiers, release labels, family count (12 other named families plus automated matches), duplication comment and homology record match the bundle. Correct inference of distant homology from a common phosphotransferase/ATPase ancestor with two-lobed cleft and ligand-induced closure; explicitly excludes transfer of substrate, reaction, kinetics, regulation, role and templates; fold-level neighbours not claimed homologous or convergent. Transparent about literature-derived mechanism. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Release (freeze date, periodic update), hierarchy, homology record, families, Pfam all supported. Lists only four of the other sibling families but that is noncentral. Correct homology-level interpretation, divergence explanation, fold caveat in both directions, explicit unsafe transfers and external evidence; honest about not retrieving quality records. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, lineage, fold description, curator comments, Pfam mappings and homology records all supported by bundle. Interprets superfamily as remote-homology inference, not proof, stronger than fold-only; rejects copper/electron-transfer transfer citing family annotations; lists structural ligand evidence, spectroscopy and redox measurements required; limits template use to fold level. Flags background-knowledge claims and unverified residue-level details. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Release, full d1ubqa_ lineage, Pfam comments, homology record, member lists and d.15 sibling superfamilies all supported by the bundle. Superfamily correctly framed as probable common origin; fold-level is weaker and not evidence of non-homology (MoaD/ThiS example handled well). Rejects transferring conjugation, Ras/Rap effector binding and p97 recruitment by name, plus within-family specificity, other-family roles (Atg8 lipidation, FERM), template and name-based transfers; external evidence listed.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5 under c.23.1 (sunids correct), superfamily-level probable common ancestry distinguished from fold similarity and from family-level closeness, explicit rejection of phosphoaspartate chemistry, kinase partnering, ODC catalysis/PLP, and KaiA clock transfer in both directions. Domain recruitment shown via 1ord three-domain split (c.23.1.4/c.67.1.5/d.125.1.1) and 1r8j (c.23.1.5 + a.186.1.1), all supported by bundle. Annotations (lacks canonical receiver features, complexed with plp, structured linker) correctly used; pretrained vs retrieved knowledge clearly separated; limits stated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Release metadata, hierarchy, 3a5c domain split (bulge inside discontinuous c.37.1.11), B chains lacking the bulge, homology record and 2.07 presence all bundle-supported. Reasoning complete: family-level homology of V1/A1 as the stronger claim, fold = similar structure not ancestry, explicitly not evidence of independent origin, function/template transfer rejected. Noncentral imprecision: describes A1 as 'archaeal or Thermus A-type' although the bundle places the Thermus domain under the V1 protein entry (310706).

Complete: three superfamilies with sunids and families all supported by bundle, homology endpoint cited correctly, within-superfamily heme-ligand note and the f.21.3 'possible link' curator comment used appropriately as an open hypothesis rather than a merger. Calibrated on both directions and lists sequence/HMM, structural-alignment, and published evolutionary evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Verified 2.08 lineage with sunids, homology scopes (sf/fa), absent warnings and superfamily annotations, all in bundle; cited example proteins (M. tuberculosis automated match, AcdA from P. horikoshii, Ktn bsu222) match retrieved nodes. Superfamily correctly identified as the deepest homology-bearing level; fold/class only structural resemblance; separate families mean no close relationship. Explicit bars on transferring substrate, reaction, NAD/NADP preference, CoA identity, residues, oligomer state, physiological role; domain-boundary caveat; notes alignments not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and sunids, deepest shared node family 100905 with 'not a true family' comment cited; explicitly says generic homology_implied_by_level does not override the curator comment; class-k homology_implied_by_level=false warning supported by bundle. Calibrated conclusion (design-level structural similarity, no evolutionary assertion, declines to call them convergent), rejects amyloid/metal transfer, notes missing alignment evidence.

Complete and bundle-supported: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 own fold vs d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 under renamed superfamily with active-site comment; retired c.137; tag domains l.1.1.1 flagged as non-biological; move located between 1.69 and 1.71 and stable through 1.75. Interprets the change as promotion from separate fold to a new family within an existing superfamily, implying probable common ancestry but not close homology; 1.69 separation was not proof of non-relation. Limits on function/template transfer and on unverified paper rationale, and correctly notes absence of homology warnings is not positive evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: correct artifact and biological lineages with bundle-matching sunids and boundaries, homology endpoint warning cited, clear statement that l-class levels carry no structural or evolutionary claim, rejection of annotation transfer through the tag, and level-stratified homology interpretation for d1a14h1 (family/superfamily/fold). States limits (no sequence or construct details retrieved). Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

States 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) persisting through 2.03, then the 2.04 split into d1acca2 A:14-225 b.179.1.1 (PA14/PA14-like, class b) and d1acca1 A:226-735 f.60.1.1, unchanged through 2.08. Correctly frames the split as a reassignment of homology claims at superfamily level only, notes PA14-like co-members (GLEYA, GH31, automated matches), refuses whole-chain function transfer, and warns that f.60's separate lineage is not a negative homology claim. Search guidance is per-domain with explicit release pinning and old-to-new sid mapping. Limits of API evidence (no curator rationale) stated.

Richest evidence: fold comment, Pfam and PubMed annotations for d.394, e.8.1.8, c.52.1.36 and c.55.3.14 all bundle-supported; correct boundaries and sccs. Strong interpretation of mosaic, superfamily-level ancestry, no function transfer, new fold not proof of no ancestor. Factual imprecision: opening states each domain sits in its own Prp8-specific family and the summary says four domains were placed as new families, but d3jb9a4 is in the pre-existing general Bromodomain family a.29.2.1 (item 2 says this correctly). Noncentral contradiction. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and well evidenced: release metadata, full lineage with sunids, lengths, both comments, the 're' domain-level flag with definition, the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 with representative-only coordinates, and the homology records. Makes the required inference that the family is defined by the repeating unit so array length reflects repeat count and construct boundaries, and that 're' records rather than contradicts this. Limits are thorough: repeat-slipped alignments, whole-domain identity inflated or diluted, stratify or exclude 're' families in benchmarks, no coordinate transfer, no RVD/target/pathogenicity transfer, curator rationale and quality data not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

All metadata correct and supported. Cites stable 2.08 with release selector; periodic label recorded as extra provenance, not a substitute. Periodic label explained as incremental update layered on 2.08 baseline, not a new stable (e.g. not 2.09), with newer structures added by automated updates. States limits of the endpoint and that 'current' moves. Meets all criteria.

Thorough and evidence-backed: unchanged a.47.2.1 lineage across 1.55/1.75/2.08; 'ms' flag added by 2.08 (absent in 1.75) with fragment comment; d1dn1b_ curated in 1.55/1.75, absent 2.03-2.05 (2.01 stated but only 2.03-2.05 in this bundle; consistent with other data), automated match to d3c98b_ from 2.06; revisions endpoint used for 2008-03-25 obsolescence. Makes the required inference that the fold rests on the complete domain, that a three-helix fragment is ambiguous (spectrin resemblance without homology or non-homology claim), that family/superfamily carry the homology claim, and that fragments should not be fold templates; explicitly states what was not retrieved (quality records, 2.01-2.07 annotations). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Excellent use of curator annotations and homology records: divergence within c.2.1 (homology_implied_by_level true), c.2 comment on similar binding modes with c.3/c.4 yet separate folds, TIM-barrel convergence labelled as the author's interpretation, explicit statement that separate placement is not proof of convergence, and complete evidence-integration list. Minor factual slip: describes the c.2.1 K+ channel NAD-binding and Rex domains as binding 'no nucleotide at all', contradicting the family name it cites. All sunids, fold cores, family list, a.100.1 and release labels supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

States 2.04 placement in different folds and superfamilies (b.23.2 under CUB-like b.23 vs b.18.1 under b.18) and 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with families still distinct (b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3). Correctly frames the 2.04 split as absence of an asserted relationship rather than proof of unrelatedness, and the merge as a curated probable-ancestry judgment. Cites the retrieved b.18.1.36 family comment (PubMed 17977833 linking d2quoa_, d1w99a3, d1nqdb_) and correctly places those domains in b.18.1.37 and b.18.1.3. Multiple evidence types given with clear separation of retrieved versus background knowledge; explicitly refuses transfer of binding specificity, Ca dependence, or insecticidal/receptor roles in either direction, and notes alignments and RMSD values were not inspected. Release and identifier detail (2.05 first move, sunid stability, chain B split with the l.1.1.1 two-residue segment) matches the bundle. Paper-title guess is explicitly hedged as unverified. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Correct release, lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, hf definition and homology flags; correctly notes d1ztra2 in class l as artifact. Quality values cited (0.00235 vs 0.442, Ramachandran -8.1) are not in this bundle but are correct release values. Reasoning complete: homology at protein level by sequence; hf exactly the similar-sequence/different-fold case; rejects template, training-positive and representative use; quality explicitly not a homology score; function transfer limited; literature mechanism flagged as unverified.

Complete: family-level homology retained, fr flag explained as 99 SEQRES vs 50 ATOM residues with range label looking complete but coordinates not; alignment coverage/normalisation bias in both directions; AEROSPACI entry-level so cannot judge completeness; d1uc6a1 the better complete domain, fragment excluded or kept only as last-resort labelled cluster member; diversity measured with complete domains, fragment marked incomplete. States what is not established (no superposition, cause of missing density). All identifiers, annotations, quality values match bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met; explicitly notes new superfamily is not a claim of analogy/independent origin; new fold is a structural claim justified only by real topology differences; placement is a revisable, manually curated hypothesis; also flags need to check boundaries and fragment/repeat/heterogeneous annotations. Release facts (2.08, 2.08-stable, periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16) and d.58 children all supported by bundle.

Families, sunids, member proteins, fold/superfamily annotations and homology record are all supported by the bundle. Justified conclusions limited to common ancestry and a shared bilobal phosphotransfer core; substrate class, regulation, inhibitors, templates, and activity all explicitly not transferable, including within-family caveat for mTOR. Evidence list covers same-family placement, residue-level alignment, specificity determinants, ligand-bound structures, assays, domain architecture, and structure-quality checks.
